questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to ﬁll in the blank and make a meaningful sentence.**

His old car ______ on the highway.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**broke down**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• '**Broke down**' is the correct phrase that means to stop working.

 
 
• **Example**- The school bus **broke down** and had to be towed to the nearest garage. 
 
 
 
• **Broke out**- (break out) means to start suddenly.
 
 
• **Example**- The crowd** broke out** in hearty laughter.
 
 
 
• **Broke in**- (break in) means to enter a building by force, especially in order to steal things.
 
 
• **Example**- A burglar **broke in** while he was asleep.
 
 
 
• **Broke up**- (break up) to end or finish.
 
 
• **Example**- The police **broke up** the fight. 
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

The driver of the car probably holds the key to ______ the crime.
questions.solution: The correct solution is option 2. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • 'Solving' is the correct option, 'holds the key to' (something) is a prepositional phrase so we will not use V1 after it i.e. 'solve', so option 4 is incorrect. • The prepositional phrase will be followed by V1+ing, so 'solving' is the correct answer. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • A prepositional phrase is a group of words consisting of a preposition, its object, and any words that modify the object. • Most of the time, a prepositional phrase modifies a verb or a noun. • These two kinds of prepositional phrases are called adverbial phrases and adjectival phrases, respectively. questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 1.

All the given options are articles. 

'The' is a definite article whereas 'an' and 'a' are definite articles. 

'An' is used if the word starts with a vowel 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u'. 'A' is used if the word starts with a consonant. 

So the most appropriate article for the blank must be 'an' because the word followed by it starts with a vowel 'i'.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.

Its a good idea to read up on a company before going for an interview.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

'Its a good idea to' is incorrect because the correct word must be 'It's a good idea'.

Its is a possessive pronoun whereas 'It's' is a contraction of 'it'.

Thus the correct sentence will be: It's a good idea to read up on a company before going for an interview.

questions.question:

• '**Coherent**' means logical and consistent. (सुसंगत)
 
 
• **Example**- *As they grow, they will struggle to learn new words, make conversation and sound **coherent**.*
 
 
 
• '**Stupid**' means having or showing a great lack of intelligence or common sense. (बेवकूफ)
 
 
• **Example**- *She angrily described her boss as a **stupid **old man.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.**

When they started, they had great ideas but lack business know-how.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** Option 2 i.e. but lack.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above-given sentence, the error is related to **tense**.
 
• It is so because **the sentence talks about the past. **
 
• Thus, the sentence should be in the** past tense.**
 
• Thus, **'lack' **should be replaced with** 'lacked'**.
 
• **Lacked **is the **past tense and past participle form **of the verb **lack**.
 
• **Lack***(verb)* - be without or deficient in.
 
 
• **For Example** - The novel **lacks **imagination.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Therefore, the correct sentence is ***When they started they had great ideas but **lacked **business know-how.*

questions.question:
**Select the antonym of the given word.**

DELICATE
questions.solution:
The correct solution is 'Firm'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• '**Delicate**' means very fine in texture or structure; of intricate workmanship or quality. (नाज़ुक, आसानी से टूट जाने वाला)

 
 
• **Example**- *He touched the **delicate **petals with gentle fingers.*
 
 
 
• The antonym of 'Delicate' is '**Firm**' which means having a solid, almost unyielding surface or structure. (He was praised for his firm leadership.)
 
 
• **Example**- *He was praised for his **firm **leadership.*
 
 
 
• '**Flimsy**' means insubstantial and vulnerable to damage. (कमज़ोर; आसानी से टूटने या फटने वाला)
 
 
• **Example**- *Snow crunched under her feet and quickly soaked her **flimsy **slippers.*
 
 
 
• '**Feeble**' means lacking physical strength, especially as a result of age or illness. (शक्तिहीन; दुर्बल, कमज़ोर)
 
 
• **Example**- *Business is suffering because of the **feeble **economy. *
 
 
 
• '**Fragile**' means easily broken or damaged. (सहज क्षतिग्रस्‍त होने या टूट जाने वाला; भंगुर)
 
 
• **Example**- *The thin glass is **fragile**. *
 
 
 
• ​Hence, the correct answer is **option 2**.

questions.question:

An introduction to a book usually stating its purpose
questions.solution:

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• '**Preface**' means an introduction to a book, typically stating its subject, scope, or aims. (पुस्‍तक के प्रतिपाद्य का लेखक द्वारा आरंभ में संक्षिप्‍त परिचय; निवेदन, प्रस्‍तावना)

 
 
• **Example**- In his **preface**, the author says that he took eight years to write the book.
 
 
 
• Here, '**Bibliography**' means a list of the books referred to in a scholarly work, typically printed as an appendix. (ग्रन्थसूची)
 
 
• **Example**- The book includes a lengthy **bibliography**.
 
 
 
• '**Acknowledgment**' means acceptance of the truth or existence of something. (किसी वस्‍तु की प्राप्ति की रसीद; पावती)
 
 
• **Example**- He's the first person mentioned in the book's **acknowledgments**. 
 
 
 
• '**Epilogue**' means a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened. (किसी पुस्‍तक, नाटक आदि का अंतवचन, उपसंहार, भरत वाक्‍य)
 
 
• **Example**- At the end of the play, the actor presented an **epilogue **to summarize the tale.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.
